Find the area $A$ bounded by the polar curve $r=2\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \pi ,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

When $r(\theta )=2\theta $, ${\theta }_{1}=0$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\pi $, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }4{\theta }^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\theta }^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2(\frac{{\theta }^{3}}{3})\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =2(\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{3})-2(\frac{{0}^{3}}{3}) \\  & =\frac{2{\pi }^{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
